soft_deny: Bash(talosctl reboot:*) -- node reboot is destructive; confirm node and mode
Bash(talosctl reset:*) -- node reset is destructive and irreversible
Bash(kubectl delete node:*) -- removing a Kubernetes node requires Longhorn CR cleanup
Bash(kubectl create:*) -- removing a Kubernetes node requires Longhorn CR cleanup
Bash(argocd app delete:*) -- deleting an ArgoCD application may destroy cluster resources
environment: ### Org-wide
**Organization**: jlaska (personal GitHub account)
**Cloud provider(s)**: Cloudflare (DNS, tunnels), Storj (S3-compatible object storage via gateway.storjshare.io), Backblaze B2 (object storage)
**Repository visibility**: private
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary

**Secrets management**: SealedSecrets (kubeseal) for Kubernetes secrets committed as `.sealed.yaml`; SOPS with age for Talos secrets (`secrets.sops.yaml`); sealed-secrets public cert at `cluster/infrastructure/sealed-secrets/cluster-cert.pem`; private key stored in Vaultwarden
**Default / protected branches**: main (no branch protection rules or rulesets listed)
**CI/CD deploy targets**: ArgoCD GitOps reconciliation to three Kubernetes clusters (Zebes K3s production, Tallon IV Talos staging, Orpheon Talos RPi 4 exit node); GitHub Actions workflows

**Network posture**: Homelab on LAN 10.0.1.0/24; external ingress via Cloudflare Tunnel (QUIC) → cloudflared → Traefik; internal ingress via Traefik internal (10.0.1.52); Tailscale mesh VPN; MetalLB L2 for LoadBalancer services

**Host containment**: None configured — assume Claude Code runs on an ordinary developer machine or CI runner with open internet; if it runs inside a container/VM/pod with an egress allow-list, no network, or neighbours it must not touch, say so here (network setting and allowed hosts, whether the cloud metadata endpoint is meant to be reachable, which cloud project/cluster/registry the task operates and as what identity). Whatever is configured, instance-metadata credential paths and node/cluster credentials of the hosting layer are never task credentials unless this entry says the agent operates that identity (see Containment Escape). The classifier sees commands, not their output, so a declared-sealed box that is actually open cannot be caught here — enforce that in network configuration.
**Source control**: jlaska/homelab on GitHub (private) and its configured remote(s) only — no additional orgs configured
**Trusted internal domains**: *.keener.us, *.internal.keener.us, garage.garage.svc.cluster.local

**Trusted cloud buckets**: speakarr-sqlite, speakarr-litestream, authentik-cnpg (config-derived — not a confirmed upload destination; uploads of local data still require confirmation), home-assistant-cnpg (config-derived — not a confirmed upload destination; uploads of local data still require confirmation), immich-cnpg (config-derived — not a confirmed upload destination; uploads of local data still require confirmation), langfuse-cnpg (config-derived — not a confirmed upload destination; uploads of local data still require confirmation), litellm-cnpg (config-derived — not a confirmed upload destination; uploads of local data still require confirmation), longhorn (config-derived — not a confirmed upload destination; uploads of local data still require confirmation), mealie-cnpg (config-derived — not a confirmed upload destination; uploads of local data still require confirmation), paperless-ngx-cnpg (config-derived — not a confirmed upload destination; uploads of local data still require confirmation), romm-cnpg (config-derived — not a confirmed upload destination; uploads of local data still require confirmation)
